abstract: High-throughput sequencing stands as a cornerstone of clinical molecular diagnostics, particularly in preimplantation genetic testing (PGT)--a key application where the selection of chromosomally normal embryos is critical to enhancing in vitro fertilization (IVF) success rates. A fundamental challenge inherent to PGT, however, lies in the ultra-low gDNA input (typically <100 pg) from embryo biopsies. To mitigate this limitation, traditional workflows rely on whole genome amplification (WGA) technologies, such as MDA, PicoPlex, and MALBAC. Yet these WGA-based protocols inherently entail pre-amplification of gDNA prior to standard library construction---a step that introduces significant coverage bias and compromised uniformity. These are intrinsic flaws irreparable by downstream library preparation or bioinformatics analysis, ultimately leading to clinical uncertainty in the interpretation of copy number variations (CNVs). In this study, we developed TUPAD (Tn5-Mediated, Uniform Pre-amplification-free and Adapter-Dimer-Free Library preparation), a transformative technology that bypasses the limitations of traditional WGA. By engineering a novel adapter-dimer-free transposon system, TUPAD enables high-efficiency library construction from as little as 1 picogram (pg) of gDNA. This breakthrough allows for a pre-amplification-free workflow, effectively eliminating the primary source of amplification bias. Compared to existing WGA standards, these advantages are fully retained in embryo biopsy and positive sample testing, TUPAD consistently generates highly uniform library data, significantly enhancing the detection limit and accuracy of CNVs and other genomic variants. Beyond these performance advantages, TUPAD also cuts wet-lab processing time by 50%. Practical validation confirms TUPAD results are stable, reliable, with proven practical utility in PGT testing.
